commands.name: 1. Native (shell) — the default
commands.description: language omitted = native: a shell line, with {{VAR}} interpolated by Kai.

commands.name: 2. Python — braces and quotes survive
commands.command:
import os
name = 'kai'
print(f"{{name}} -> {name}")
print('{{GREETING}} is NOT interpolated; the variable is in the environment:', os.environ['GREETING'])
print("quotes ' \" $HOME `ls` ünïcödé ✓")
commands.description: The code reaches python3 untouched: f-string braces, quotes, $ and backticks are safe. GREETING arrives through os.environ.

commands.name: 3. Python — stdin is free
commands.description: No `python3 -c` quoting, and input() works: type the answer in the output panel's input field.

commands.name: 4. Python — parameter as an environment variable
commands.description: Parameters arrive as environment variables, like everything else.

commands.name: 5. Node — top-level await
commands.description: Node code runs inside an async function, so await works at the top level. PORT comes from process.env.

commands.name: 6. Python — custom interpreter
commands.description: The interpreter is a shell line: this one has arguments (like `uv run python` would). Empty = the global one from Settings → Languages.

commands.name: 7. Node — talk to the Kai app (kai module)
commands.description: The global `kai` object: sends a tray notification, lists the environments and the registered commands. Needs the Kai app running (it is the app that runs this, so it is).

commands.name: 8. Showcase (Python: kip + kai modules)
commands.description: A long interactive Python program: a menu you keep returning to, a 4-step wizard with Back, dependent fields, chips, validation, checklist and retry, plus tools that use the kai module (environments, processes, notifications, run another command). The program lives in showcase.py; you can also paste its content into the command field.
